_about: What SIXDOGS actually runs on, what it costs, and what is still pending. This is the operational source of truth, kept up to date as things get set up or change. community.json holds what PLAYERS see; this holds what the OWNER is paying for and running. The bill shown on the website and in #support-the-community is derived from `services` below, so it can never drift from reality: add a service here and it appears in both. Never put passwords, tokens or account credentials in this file. The repo is public.

services.name: Game server
services.notes: RCON is enabled and reachable. Build ++Wardogs+Live-CL-501228. Public address 64.87.44.73:20016. CONFIRMED 2026-09-21: /server reports the RCON host as 64.87.44.73, the same machine, so the address points at the right box. The public address is kept here for reference but is no longer shown on the website: players use the Server ID with Join by ID.

services.name: Bot hosting
services.what: Runs the Discord bot, core and the Postgres database
services.plan: Hobby, with a Postgres database attached
services.notes: Hobby, $5/month including $5 of usage, confirmed by the owner. The Postgres service counts toward the same usage, so watch the Usage page if the bot grows. CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 via /server: DATABASE_URL is set and core is on Railway Postgres, so links, ratings and match history survive restarts and deploys.

services.name: Domain
services.notes: Billed yearly and shown on the bill as a per-month share. Confirmed by the owner.

services.name: Website hosting
services.what: Serves sixdogs.gg and rebuilds it on every push
services.notes: Free plan covers this comfortably. DNS for the domain is also Cloudflare, also free. The Pages project is Git-connected and rebuilds on every push to main, replacing an earlier Direct Upload project that never rebuilt and left the site a day stale while everything else worked. Every page carries <meta name="sixdogs-build"> with the commit it was built from, and the browser console prints it, so a stale deploy is visible at a glance.

services.name: Live status
services.what: Cloudflare Worker at live.sixdogs.gg that holds the latest server summary for the website
services.notes: Worker "sixdogs-live", KV namespace "sixdogs-live" (6215eeaf827f4ba8be91f231f2b06e00) bound as STATUS, PUSH_TOKEN secret, custom domain live.sixdogs.gg. Set up by the owner 2026-09-21, along with STATUS_PUSH_URL and STATUS_PUSH_TOKEN in Railway. Serves the root and /status alike. Claude cannot reach the domain from its sandbox, so confirm by opening it.

pending.what: A way to actually give a donor their reserved slot. /reserved can read the list, but the live build offers no route to write it, so a slot has to be added in the settings document via PUT /v1/config, which is not implemented.
pending.blocking: The donation page promises "$10 or more: a reserved slot for that month". The mechanism is now known and written up in docs/wardogs-rcon.md: the slots are an array in the game session section of the settings, capped at 6. What is missing is a list editor. setConfigValue changes one Key=Value and refuses list lines on purpose, so appending a SteamID needs its own equally careful function and its own tests.
pending.howTo: See docs/wardogs-rcon.md for the exact key. Write a list editor beside setConfigValue: append or remove one member, keep the ClearArray directive first, refuse duplicates and refuse to go past the cap. Then the same read/validate/If-Match write path the single-value change already uses. Check the result with /reserved.

pending.what: Decide and set MinimumRequiredPlayers (currently 20) so the game server and SEED_TARGET agree, and find out whether an AFK kick timeout exists at all.
pending.blocking: SEED_TARGET is 45 and the server starts a match at 20, so the two disagree: the server starts matches long before seeding would call anyone in, which makes the call-in pointless. They have to be the same number. Which number is the owner's call and depends on how big the Discord is, since a threshold nobody can reach means no matches at all.
pending.howTo: Set it with /settings section:MatchState.PreMatch.WaitingForPlayers.PlayerCount key:MinimumRequiredPlayers value:<n> confirm:True, and set SEED_TARGET to the same number in Railway. For the AFK timeout, read the four sections nobody has looked at yet; it may not be a server setting on this build.

decisions: Railway over a plain VPS: no SSH for routine changes, settings are a web form, managed Postgres, and it redeploys on every push to main.
Cloudflare Pages over Railway for the website: free, purpose-built for static files, and the _redirects file and the live-status worker were already written for it.
Postgres on Railway rather than the embedded PGlite: PGlite measured about 500 MB resident, which is most of a small box.
Push straight to main, no pull requests: solo project, and main is what deploys.

Seeding pings an opt-in role (Match Alerts), never @everyone, at most once every SEED_COOLDOWN_MINUTES, and never for fewer than SEED_MIN_PLEDGES people. The owner asked for a limit so people aren't pinged continuously; the default is 45 minutes rather than 3, because the list is emptied when a ping fires, so a second ping needs a fresh set of people anyway.

Seeding is a standing list, and a name is never removed because that person went to wait in the server. The owner hit this within minutes of the first version: he clicked, went to warm up in game, and disappeared off his own list. Wanting to play and being in the server are the same intention. The board shows everyone on the list, not a sample, because seeing your own name is the confirmation that the click worked.

Two seeding messages, not one: a heads-up at SEED_NUDGE_AT (10) carrying the running count to recruit more people, and the call-in at SEED_TARGET (45). They keep separate cooldowns so the recruiting message can never block the match it recruited for.

rules: Never move players between teams automatically during a match. The owner has ruled this out: /move stays an admin command only, and no balancing rule may ever call it on its own.

Reserved slots: any donation gets the Supporter role, $10 or more gets a reserved slot for that month. There are six. If more than six donors want in at once they wait; do not add caveats about this to the public wording.
Nobody is pinged who didn't ask to be. The seeding call-in mentions the opt-in Match Alerts role only, and the bot never uses @everyone or @here.
